prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0074: The IMPACT POC prepares a comprehensive report that documents all identified risk metrics and how they are affected by CO2 levels, specific mass/volume allocations, and the specific choice of configuration of the ECLSS, with and without the new technology.
U0075: Using this information, the HRP Elements provide their input for updating the CO2 exposure standards.
U0076: SCENARIO 5: SCENARIO REQUIREMENTS DEVELOPMENT Stakeholders: Mars Program CHP System Management Life Cycle Phase: Phase A Mars Program CHP System Management needs to identify the most appropriate medical system requirements for an upcoming mission to Mars.
U0077: The CHP Systems Engineering Team uses IMPACT to help define these requirements by analyzing a Mars Medical System Concept of Operations and the appropriate Mars-based AMCL, an IMPACT-based product, with associated medical capabilities.
U0078: Once formulated, the CHP Systems Engineering Team uses IMPACT’s medical system modeling tool to capture and analyze the medical requirements.
U0079: The requirements are then sent to Mars Program CHP System Management for approval.
U0080: SCENARIO 6: TRADE ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY SYSTEM RESOURCES Stakeholders: Exploration Program CHP System Management, Exploration Program Management Life Cycle Phase: Phase B/C The Exploration Program CHP System Management is starting to develop requirements, designs, and hardware for a new exploration vehicle’s medical system, and they want to use IMPACT to determine what resources they should include in the medical system.
U0081: The CHP System Management contacts the IMPACT POC, and they perform a trade study on the mission constraints that the CHP System Management proposes.
U0082: IMPACT provides a candidate medical system that meets the mass and volume constraints, but the CHP System Management is not satisfied because the proposed medical system is below the mass constraint by 1 kg.
U0083: The CHP System Management wants to run IMPACT again to see what the medical risk would be if that 1 kg was filled with medications or an automated external defibrillator (AED) capability.
U0084: The IMPACT POC runs these two different scenarios and provides the results to the CHP System Management.
U0085: With the inclusion of an AED, IMPACT removes some of the other medical capabilities.
U0086: With the inclusion of just medications, the AED capability is missing.
U0087: The CHP System Management analyzes these runs and decides to add the AED to the originally proposed medical system.
U0088: This makes the total mass and volume larger than the original constraints set by the Exploration Program Management.
U0089: The CHP System Management provides the Exploration Program Management with rationale documented as to why they wish to include the AED even though it makes the system more massive than originally intended.
U0090: The Exploration Program Management and the CHP System Management then negotiate on mass, volume, and risk to identify the final system that will be designated for the exploration vehicle’s medical system.
U0091: SCENARIO 7: UPDATED RISK IMPACT JUST PRIOR TO MISSION Stakeholders: Mars Program Management, MedOps Life Cycle Phase: Phase D The Physician Astronaut on a mission to Mars gets sick just prior to launch.
U0092: The backup crew is initiated and the crew launch on time to maintain the narrow launch window.
U0093: The Mars Program Management wants to understand how this change impacts the risk for LOCL and QTL during the transit phase of the mission, since the primary Physician Astronaut was trained in emergency medicine and the backup crewmember was trained as a primary care physician.
U0094: MedOps wants to understand how the execution of planned and unplanned medical activities will be affected.
U0095: They use IMPACT to determine how the difference in knowledge, ability, and skills between the primary and backup crew will affect medical risk.
U0096: The output they receive indicates that, while there are no sufficient changes to LOCL if certain conditions were to occur during their 3-year mission, there are significant changes to QTL.
U0097: IMPACT indicates that the gap in the risk can be reduced by up-linking knowledge augmentation references, certain just-in-time training modules, and a couple specific procedures so that the newly initiated Physician Astronaut can be able to implement the necessary medical intervention if needed during the mission.
U0098: With these provisions in place, IMPACT shows that the risk for QTL can successfully be reduced to an acceptable level by the time the crew reaches the transit phase of the mission.
